input.body:
Step 3's flip, from the #801 plan — **approval №2**. Merging this moves every member to the work-item queue on its next converge.

It is deliberately **not** the whole of PR‑2: the slot deletion cannot ride with it, for a reason I found in the code rather than in the plan. That is the main thing to review here.

## The flip

`dispatchMode` now answers `queue` for an absent setting, and `slots` only when a repo asks for it by name. So the flip needs **no migration record and no edit to any file a member owns** — which is the standing *"a pack default stays in the pack — don't ask it at adoption, don't write it into a member's config"* ruling applied to the migration itself. Fourteen declarations do not have to be rewritten, and there is no fielded-worker-versus-fresh-canon skew to reason about.

Three callers were re-deriving the mode from the config key rather than asking `dispatchMode` — `run.mjs`, the janitor worker, and `stubFor`. They had to collapse onto the one function first: a default cannot be changed while the rule lives in four places. The canon's own `.claudinite-checks.json` drops `"dispatch": "queue"`, since stating a default is the thing that later drifts from it (patched as anchored text, not re-serialized).

## Why the slot machinery must not go in this PR

The plan says *"slot machinery deleted in this same PR"*. Two facts make that unsafe:

1. **The engine converge replaces the mount wholesale** — `updates/engine-update.mjs` `rmSync`s `.claudinite/shared/engine` and re-copies. A file canon deletes is gone from every member's mount on its next converge, whatever that member's config says.
2. **`.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push.** The engine flow runs with `workflows: false` and `env: {}` (*"this process cannot deliver a workflow file"*); the content is staged to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` and landed by the apply stage over MCP.

And the two stubs call **different entry points**:

```
claudinite-scheduler.yml → node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/run.mjs
claudinite-tick.yml      → node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/tick.mjs
```

So a release that deleted slots would leave every member whose workflow had not yet been landed running an hourly cron against a file its mount no longer contains. That is not a degraded state, it is the **non-self-healing** one: the thing that would deliver the corrected workflow is the apply stage of an update, and the scheduler that runs it is what just died. Same shape as the #651/#652 wedge, self-inflicted.

Keeping the slot code makes the same window **benign** — `run.mjs` sees queue mode and no-ops — and this PR also makes it **loud**. Reaching that branch at all proves the workflow is still the slot shim, since the tick's workflow never enters `run.mjs`; so it now says exactly that and names the remedy, rather than exiting green having done nothing:

```
- this project dispatches through the work-item queue — the slot scheduler evaluates nothing here
! this run came from the SLOT workflow, so this repo's .github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml
  has not been converged to the tick yet — nothing is dispatched until it is
  fix: land the staged workflows in .claudinite/pending-workflows/ …
```

**Deletion belongs in a follow-up PR, once every member is confirmed on the queue** — same day, so the no-lingering-legacy discipline still holds; just not in an order that can strand a member.

## Verification

- Full suite: **1778 pass, 0 fail**. Three tests failed first and are updated rather than worked around — each was a fixture that meant "a default member" and now means "a queue member"; they now say which they mean, and `dispatchMode`'s test pins the new default in both directions.
- Sweep: **0 blocking, 59 advisory** against `main`'s 58. The one addition is `file-placement` on the new import in `pack-update.mjs`, the same class its six neighbouring dynamic imports of that module already carry.

Not verified here: a real member converging. No member has run a cycle against this, and the first that does is the evidence — which is why the per-member burst is the next checklist item on #801 rather than something this PR claims.

Refs #801

https://claude.ai/code/session_01DJxMKHSzrPAi3ayvhS6NHv

### Step 3's flip is up as #888 — and it splits PR‑2 in two

The flip half is ready. The **slot deletion cannot ride with it**, and the reason is in the code rather than the plan:

- `updates/engine-update.mjs` **replaces the mount wholesale** (`rmSync` + re-copy), so a file canon deletes leaves every member's mount on its next converge regardless of that member's config.
- `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push — the engine flow runs `workflows: false`, `env: {}`, and the content is staged for the apply stage.
- The two stubs call **different entry points**: `run.mjs` vs `queue/tick.mjs`.

So deleting slots in the same release strands any member whose workflow has not yet been landed: its hourly cron runs a file the mount no longer has, and the apply stage that would fix it is work the dead scheduler dispatches. Non-self-healing, and the same shape as the #651/#652 wedge.

Keeping the slot code makes that window benign (`run.mjs` no-ops) — and #888 makes it **loud**, since reaching that branch at all proves the workflow is still the slot shim.

**Proposed amendment to this plan:** PR‑2 becomes two PRs — the flip (#888), then deletion once every member is confirmed on the queue. Same day, so no-lingering-legacy still holds; just not in an order that can strand a member. The Step 3 checklist above reads as one PR and should be read as two.
